title: The naive framing: "does a plugin make Claude smarter?"
text: People think installing a plugin just makes Claude smarter, more facts, same generalist. That's not it. A plugin makes Claude an equipped specialist. So, what does a plugin actually make Claude?

title: A smart friend, not an accountant — the anchor
text: Claude without plugins is a capable generalist. It can discuss any topic and apply broad knowledge to your situation. Useful, but it's a smart friend helping with your taxes. They'll try. They're not an accountant. A plugin makes Claude

title: One well, dug deep
text: The accountant, or the marketer, the sales researcher, the contract reviewer. It trades a mile of shallow knowledge for a well that goes deep in one domain. It's tempting to think that's just a

title: Not just a smarter prompt — the wrong guess
text: Smarter prompt, more details stuffed into the same conversation. But a prompt can't log into your CRM, add a slash command shortcut to your menu, or hand a multi-step job to a coordinating sub-agent. A plugin does all three. Skills are the expertise, methodical

title: Expertise, auto-armed — skills
text: Frameworks, not generic tips. They switch on automatically when they're relevant. Ask a marketing question with marketing installed and Claude just reaches for them.

title: Reach into your tools — connectors
text: Connectors are the reach. The sales plugin into your CRM, the data plugin into your spreadsheets, so Claude works on your actual business data, not hypothetical examples.

title: One slash, one job — commands
text: Commands are the shortcuts. {slash} prospect brief and sales research is a company. {slash} audit and marketing tears apart a page. Type {slash} inside Coward to see them all. Sub-agents are

title: Many steps, one answer — subagents
text: The autonomy. Ask finance to build a model and it quietly coordinates the steps, gather, structure, run scenarios, compile, so you get one clean result instead of a jumble. That's the shift in one line. General

title: Knowing becomes doing
text: Knowledge becomes contextual capability. Legal reviews the actual contract you're about to sign. Marketing drafts in your brand voice from your real style guide, not a hypothetical example. Back to that friend and the accountant.

title: The friend, and the pro — the anchor returns
text: It's the difference between asking a well-read friend what to watch for in a contract and asking someone who reviews contracts for a living. That's the whole reason a plugin is worth your time. Anthropic released these as open source.

title: Open, so it bends
text: For you that mostly means free, no charge beyond your paid plan. But open buys three more things. Transparency instead of a black box, community fixes over time, and the ability to adjust a plug-in that almost fits. Out of the box, the sales plug-in is

title: Configured hits harder
text: Useful. Configured with your process, your qualifying criteria, your positioning, it's dramatically more powerful. Customization is the next chapter, and that's where the real gain shows up. Four limits stated plainly, plug-ins don't hand Claude perfect

title: Four hard limits
text: Judgment. They don't bypass its knowledge boundaries. They work only inside your existing access, your credentials, your permissions, nothing new. And they're tools, not replacements. Legal flags a scary clause, it can't weigh it against the deal. Finance builds the model, it can't tell you the

title: You keep the judgment
text: Assumptions fit your industry. Human judgment stays on the consequential calls. That caveat isn't a disclaimer to skip, it's the instructions. You don't need the whole catalog, most people run two or three. Start with your primary function, whatever you spend

title: Two or three — choosing yours
text: Your day on. Add your biggest bottleneck, the thing you know you should do but don't. Then keep productivity running underneath as the foundation. A plug-in doesn't make Claude know more, it makes Claude equipped. Tools, reach, and shortcuts on your own work, with the judgment still yours. Your turn. Paste this into Claude. I run

text: A small business and I'm new to Claude plug-ins. Walk me through choosing my first two. Ask what I do all day, name

title: Your turn
text: The function I keep neglecting, then tell me which plug-in to install first, which second, and one way to customize each for my business. Claude equipped with a Claude plug-in actually gives you. Liam in for Bear.
